drafted_from: tool:find-beats's own row in tools/media-composition/tool-rows.json, tools/media-composition/do-work/detect-beats.mjs, and the script run on a synthetic 8 second clip with a click every half second
start_here: Say to your AI: "Find the beats in the music of my video so I can cut on them." It runs tool:find-beats and hands back each beat time in seconds.
no_lists_because: It reads one video you name by its file identity and answers from that video alone, so it keeps no list of its own.
instructions: 1. Find the identity of the song or the video with the soundtrack in your files: 1f: then 64 hex.
2. Say "Find the beats in this video" with that identity; the tool takes no other input.

3. The AI calls run_resource_operation at @workshop-tools with method tools:run and tool tool:find-beats. The door runs it in a container and answers {"result": {...}}; an error comes back as {"error": "what to change"}.
4. Read result.beats (seconds) and result.count; the answer also carries bpm, the tempo from the median gap between beats. Cut your clips on those times.

worked_examples.title: Clicks every half second found as beats
worked_examples.ask: Find the beats in my video.
worked_examples.given: read from tools/media-composition/do-work/detect-beats.mjs and run on an 8 second clip with a loud 50 millisecond click every 0.5 seconds (a true 120 beats a minute)
